vocabulary_scope: Expanded Practical Conversational, Emergency, Healthcare & Travel Vocabulary (28 Verified Entries)
disclaimer: This is a curated, verified baseline vocabulary for practical communication and demonstration based on official ISLRTC documentation. Note: Indian Sign Language uses visual-spatial grammar with Topic-Comment and Wh-final syntax, which does not follow spoken English or Hindi word order.

data_attribution.primary_reference: ISLRTC (Indian Sign Language Research and Training Centre) Standard Dictionary guidelines & Consented Open Benchmark Annotations
data_attribution.consent_status: Consented benchmark coordinate references; zero private biometric video retained

signs.meaning: Traditional respectful greeting, hello, or welcome.
signs.hand_configuration: Both palms pressed together vertically at chest height (Anjali Mudra) or open dominant palm forward greeting wave.
signs.isl_grammar_structure: Used at opening of discourse; can be accompanied by polite head tilt.
signs.cultural_linguistic_notes: Namaste is deeply rooted in Indian cultural deaf signing as both greeting and formal acknowledgment of presence.

media.description: Both palms joined vertically in front of chest.

signs.meaning: Inquiry regarding personal wellbeing and health.
signs.hindi_text: आप कैसे हैं? / क्या हाल है?
signs.hand_configuration: Pointing forward to person (YOU), followed by both open palms twisting inward to outward with inquiring facial expression (HOW).
signs.isl_grammar_structure: ISL Syntax: [YOU] [HOW?] (Wh-interrogative question structure; question particle occurs sentence-finally with non-manual furrowed eyebrows).
signs.cultural_linguistic_notes: English word order 'How are you' is inverted in authentic ISL to 'YOU HOW?' to establish subject focus first.

media.description: Index point to conversational partner followed by dual palm twist and inquiring brow.

signs.meaning: Asking for someone's name or sign name.
signs.hand_configuration: Open palm towards conversational partner (YOUR), two fingers of dominant hand tapping opposite fingers (NAME), then open questioning hand (WHAT?).
signs.isl_grammar_structure: ISL Syntax: [YOUR] [NAME] [WHAT?] (Wh-question: WHAT occurs at the end of the sentence with furrowed brows).
signs.cultural_linguistic_notes: In the deaf community, asking someone's name often leads to fingerspelling the legal name followed by their community Sign Name (name sign).

media.description: Pointing forward, tapping name index fingers, ending with Wh-question hand gesture.

signs.meaning: Courteous expression of pleasure upon meeting someone.
signs.hand_configuration: Both index fingers pointing upwards approaching each other from opposite sides until touching (MEET), followed by flat hand circling heart or thumbs up (HAPPY/GOOD).
signs.isl_grammar_structure: ISL Syntax: [MEET] [HAPPY] (Spatial classifier movement where two upright indices represent people converging).
signs.cultural_linguistic_notes: The convergence of index fingers spatializes two individuals meeting in physical space.

media.description: Two upright index fingers meet in center, followed by happy chest gesture.

signs.meaning: Expression of gratitude and appreciation.
signs.hand_configuration: Flat dominant hand with fingers together; fingertips touch chin/lips and move forward towards the other person.
signs.isl_grammar_structure: Directional sign: originates at signer's face and directs towards recipient.
signs.cultural_linguistic_notes: Direct visual eye contact is mandatory while producing this sign in ISL.

media.description: Flat hand moves forward from chin level towards the recipient.

signs.meaning: Polite request.
signs.hand_configuration: Open flat palm facing inward rubbed in gentle clockwise circular motion over chest/heart area.
signs.isl_grammar_structure: Precedes or succeeds request with polite non-manual head nod.
signs.cultural_linguistic_notes: Indicates humility and sincere request in Indian signing context.

media.description: Flat palm placed on chest moving in gentle circular motion.

signs.meaning: Warm reception or welcoming response to thank you.
signs.hand_configuration: Both hands held open, palms facing inward/upward, sweeping towards signer in inviting motion.
signs.isl_grammar_structure: Inviting spatial motion accompanied by a warm smile.
signs.cultural_linguistic_notes: Reflects the traditional Indian concept of 'Atithi Devo Bhava' (Guest is divine).

media.description: Open arms and hands sweeping inward in inviting greeting.

signs.meaning: Expression of regret, apology, or sympathy.
signs.hand_configuration: Closed fist with knuckles facing chest rubbed in circular motion over heart with apologetic facial expression.
signs.isl_grammar_structure: Accompanied by non-manual regret markers: slight head bow and lowered brows.
signs.cultural_linguistic_notes: Essential social repair sign in deaf conversational interactions.

media.description: Fist rubbing over chest in apologetic circular motion.

signs.meaning: Male parent.
signs.hand_configuration: Index finger or thumb strokes mustache line above lip or taps side of upper cheek.
signs.isl_grammar_structure: Noun: placed in topic position in family descriptions.
signs.cultural_linguistic_notes: In ISL, masculine family signs are traditionally localized in the upper face/mustache region.

media.description: Hand tracing mustache line above lip indicating male elder.

signs.meaning: Female parent.
signs.hand_configuration: Index and middle finger (or nose ring touch) gently tapping lower cheek or chin line.
signs.isl_grammar_structure: Noun: placed in topic position in sentence.
signs.cultural_linguistic_notes: In ISL, feminine family signs are traditionally localized in the lower cheek, nose-stud, or earlobe area.

media.description: Fingers tapping cheek/chin indicating female parent.

signs.meaning: Household group, relatives, or immediate family members.
signs.hand_configuration: Both hands form curved C or F shapes starting together in center, drawing an outward circle and touching pinkies together.
signs.isl_grammar_structure: Collective noun denoting inclusive social unit.
signs.cultural_linguistic_notes: The circular enclosure represents the protected household envelope.

media.description: Both hands drawing an inclusive circle joining together.

signs.meaning: Food, meals, eating, or being hungry.
signs.hand_configuration: Fingertips and thumb of dominant hand brought together pointing upwards, brought repeatedly towards mouth.
signs.isl_grammar_structure: Noun and verb share same base handshape (FOOD vs EAT distinguished by repetition).
signs.cultural_linguistic_notes: Represents traditional Indian eating with fingers.

media.description: Clustered fingertips tap towards the mouth in eating motion.

signs.meaning: Drinking water or being thirsty.
signs.hand_configuration: Thumb and index finger curved like a cup or 'W' handshape held near the mouth and tilted.
signs.isl_grammar_structure: Can combine with 'WANT' or 'WHERE' in two-sign queries.
signs.cultural_linguistic_notes: Foundational emergency and daily living sign across all Indian states.

media.description: Curved hand forming a cup tilted towards the mouth.

signs.meaning: Hot tea beverage.
signs.hand_configuration: Non-dominant hand forms saucer or cup; dominant hand with thumb and index pinched dips repeatedly into cup like dipping teabag/sugar.
signs.isl_grammar_structure: Common conversational offering in Indian hospitality context.
signs.cultural_linguistic_notes: Chai is universally understood across Indian deaf culture as a social gesture.

media.description: Pinching fingers dip into saucer cup in tea drinking motion.

signs.meaning: Feeling hunger or needing food.
signs.hand_configuration: Dominant curved hand tracing downward from throat to stomach with tense facial expression.
signs.isl_grammar_structure: Predicate adjective; often combined with [FOOD] [WANT].
signs.cultural_linguistic_notes: The downward motion directly indicates an empty stomach.

media.description: Curved hand tracing down chest towards stomach indicating hunger.

signs.meaning: Request for assistance, medical support, or emergency aid.
signs.hand_configuration: Non-dominant flat palm facing upward; dominant hand forms thumbs-up fist placed on palm and lifted upward together.
signs.isl_grammar_structure: Directional verb: moving towards recipient means 'I help you'; moving towards self means 'You help me'.
signs.cultural_linguistic_notes: Crucial high-priority sign in hospital, transit, and emergency encounters.

media.description: Fist resting on flat palm lifted upward together.

signs.meaning: Urgent request for immediate emergency assistance.
signs.english_text: I need help / Please help me
signs.hindi_text: मुझे मदद चाहिए / कृपया सहायता करें
signs.hand_configuration: Point to chest (ME), lift fist on flat palm moving towards chest (HELP-ME), combined with urgent wide-eyed facial expression.
signs.isl_grammar_structure: ISL Syntax: [ME] [HELP-TOWARDS-ME] [URGENT] (Directional verb incorporates beneficiary pronoun).
signs.cultural_linguistic_notes: Direction of the lift indicates that the signer is the beneficiary of the urgent assistance.

media.description: Directional help sign lifted towards chest with urgent facial expression.

signs.meaning: Medical doctor or physician.
signs.hand_configuration: Two fingers of dominant hand gently tapping inner wrist of non-dominant arm as if checking pulse.
signs.isl_grammar_structure: Noun: occurs in topic or locative questions (e.g. DOCTOR WHERE?).
signs.cultural_linguistic_notes: Universally recognized in ISL based on the diagnostic act of taking pulse (naadi).

media.description: Two fingers tapping wrist pulse area indicating doctor.

signs.meaning: Hospital, clinic, or medical facility.
signs.hand_configuration: Dominant index and middle fingers draw a vertical line and cross bar (cross symbol) on the upper non-dominant arm or shoulder.
signs.isl_grammar_structure: Locative noun; commonly preceded by [GO] or followed by [WHERE?].
signs.cultural_linguistic_notes: Derived from the Red Cross emblem recognized in emergency medical services.

media.description: Drawing cross shape on upper arm indicating hospital facility.

signs.meaning: Physical pain, hurt, ache, or illness.
signs.hand_configuration: Both index fingers pointing towards each other and twisting inward/outward near the location of pain, with grimacing facial expression.
signs.isl_grammar_structure: Spatialized verb/noun: produced near body region experiencing pain (head for headache, stomach for stomachache).
signs.cultural_linguistic_notes: Facial grimace (non-manual marker) indicates severity of pain.

media.description: Twisting index fingers towards each other with pain expression.

signs.meaning: Toilet, washroom, or bathroom facility.
signs.hand_configuration: Dominant hand forms T-handshape (thumb tucked under index finger) or small finger extended, shaking side to side gently.
signs.isl_grammar_structure: Often combined with [WHERE?] in travel environments.
signs.cultural_linguistic_notes: Standard public transit and airport facility request sign.

media.description: T-handshape oscillating side to side.

signs.meaning: Inquiry about physical location or direction.
signs.hand_configuration: Both hands held open at waist height, palms facing upwards, moving horizontally side to side with furrowed brows.
signs.isl_grammar_structure: ISL Wh-interrogative syntax: occurs at sentence end (e.g. [TRAIN] [WHERE?], [TOILET] [WHERE?]).
signs.cultural_linguistic_notes: Furrowed eyebrows and squinted eyes are mandatory non-manual markers for Wh-questions in ISL.

media.description: Open upward palms oscillating side to side with questioning brow.

signs.meaning: Command to cease action, halt, or pause.
signs.hand_configuration: Dominant hand open, fingers straight together, palm facing straight ahead at shoulder height.
signs.isl_grammar_structure: Imperative command; sudden emphatic halt.
signs.cultural_linguistic_notes: Universally understood safety stop signal.

media.description: Open vertical palm held firmly outward.

signs.meaning: Affirmative agreement or consent.
signs.hand_configuration: Dominant hand closed into a fist (S-handshape), nodding up and down from the wrist like a head nod.
signs.isl_grammar_structure: Affirmative particle accompanied by head nod.
signs.cultural_linguistic_notes: Simulates head nodding using hand motion.

media.description: Fist nods vertically simulating an agreement nod.

signs.meaning: Negative response, refusal, or disagreement.
signs.hand_configuration: Index and middle fingers extended together with thumb, snapping shut or index finger wagging horizontally.
signs.isl_grammar_structure: Negative particle accompanied by head shake.
signs.cultural_linguistic_notes: Two-finger snap is standard fast conversational negation in ISL.

media.description: Extended index and middle finger closing against thumb.

signs.meaning: Positive evaluation, good condition, or approval.
signs.hand_configuration: Dominant hand forms a clear upright thumbs-up gesture in front of body.
signs.isl_grammar_structure: Evaluative adjective.
signs.cultural_linguistic_notes: Standard positive affirmation sign across urban and regional ISL dialects.

media.description: Clear thumbs-up gesture.

signs.meaning: Negative evaluation, illness, distress, or disapproval.
signs.hand_configuration: Dominant hand forms a clear thumbs-down gesture pointing towards the floor.
signs.isl_grammar_structure: Negative evaluative adjective accompanied by frown.
signs.cultural_linguistic_notes: Standard negation/evaluation sign.

media.description: Clear thumbs-down gesture.

signs.meaning: Request for an additional quantity or repetition.
signs.hand_configuration: Both hands form flattened-O shapes (fingertips touching thumbs) and tap together at fingertips repeatedly.
signs.isl_grammar_structure: Quantifier modifying preceding noun or standalone request.
signs.cultural_linguistic_notes: Common in meal requests and learning environments.

media.description: Both hands with fingertips touching thumbs tapping together.
